abstract: Background/Objectives: Irinotecan is a component of standard first-line regimens for advanced pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), yet cells that survive irinotecan treatment may retain the capacity to re-establish growth. Most anticancer drug screens use short-term growth inhibition as an initial criterion for compound selection, potentially excluding compounds with limited acute activity. We asked whether some of these excluded candidates might nevertheless show substantial long-term activity and enhance irinotecan responses in combination. Methods: We first screened 3524 compounds for short-term growth inhibition and advanced compounds with limited acute activity to a 10-day colony-growth screen. Long-term hits were narrowed to clinically relevant anticancer agents and then screened with irinotecan. Talazoparib showed the lowest combination-to-single-agent score and was selected for further evaluation. The combination was evaluated across multiple BRCA1/2-wild-type PDAC cell lines and further validated using additional PARP inhibitors and a xenograft model. RNA sequencing and γH2AX analysis were used to examine associated DNA damage-response features. Results: Of the 1877 compounds advanced from the initial 3-day screen, 334 (17.8%) met the long-term hit criterion. In short- versus long-term comparisons, irinotecan plus talazoparib produced greater growth suppression and higher Bliss synergy scores in 10-day than in 72 h assays. Enhanced long-term responses were observed across five BRCA1/2-wild-type PDAC cell lines, and similar long-term effects were observed with three additional PARP inhibitors. The combination also showed synergistic antitumor activity in an MIA PaCa-2 subcutaneous xenograft model. Transcriptomic and γH2AX analyses provided findings consistent with replication-stress and DNA-damage-response processes. Conclusions: A substantial subset of compounds with limited acute activity showed substantial long-term activity. PARP inhibition enhanced irinotecan responses and emerged as a candidate combination strategy in BRCA1/2-wild-type PDAC.
key_points_ko: 초기 3일 스크리닝을 통과한 1877개 화합물 중 334개(17.8%)가 장기 효과 기준을 충족했습니다.
Talazoparib와 irinotecan 병용은 72시간보다 10일 배양 검사에서 더 큰 성장 억제와 높은 시너지 점수를 나타냈습니다.
이러한 장기 병용 효과는 5개의 BRCA1/2 야생형 췌관선암 세포주와 MIA PaCa-2 이종이식(xenograft) 모델에서 확인되었습니다.
summary_ko: 이 연구는 급성 활성은 낮지만 장기적인 억제 효과를 보이는 화합물을 찾기 위해 3524개 화합물을 스크리닝했습니다. 그 결과 급성기에는 효과가 제한적이었던 talazoparib(탈라조파립) 등의 PARP 억제제가 irinotecan(이리노테칸)과의 병용에서 우수한 장기 억제 효과를 보였습니다. 이러한 병용 효과는 BRCA1/2 야생형(wild-type) 췌관선암(PDAC) 세포주와 동물 모델(xenograft model)에서 확인되었습니다. RNA 시퀀싱 및 γH2AX 분석을 통해 DNA 손상 반응과 복제 스트레스 관련 기전이 확인되었습니다.
title: Long-Term Drug Screening Identifies PARP Inhibitors as Irinotecan Combination Partners in BRCA1/2-Wild-Type Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma
title_ko: 장기 약물 스크리닝을 통해 BRCA1/2 야생형 췌관선암에서 irinotecan 병용 파트너로 PARP 억제제 발굴
